title: Daniels et al. v. Nashville Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint found moot by the SJC; no merits ruling or relief. A six-member dissent would not declare mootness, noting no record evidence of abandonment or withdrawal and that a disputed filing-timeliness question should have been handled by a panel; the majority supplied no rationale.
first_summary: The SJC declared Case 2016-13 moot because circumstances had changed, so it did not answer the complaint against Nashville Presbytery over its ruling that a session erred and had to redress its actions. Six commissioners dissented, arguing complainants had not abandoned their complaint, the filing-timeliness question should have been resolved by a panel, and mootness without record support was improper. No merits relief was granted.
summary: The dissent describes the underlying dispute: session and congregation members complained that Nashville Presbytery improperly ruled their session had erred and had to redress its actions. The SJC, without explaining its reasoning, declared the complaint moot because circumstances had changed, leaving the merits unanswered. The dissent objected that the record showed no withdrawal or abandonment, that any filing-timeliness dispute should go to a panel, and that unexplained mootness undermines review. No relief was granted.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: SJC decision on complaint, Case 2016-13, dated August 30, 2017, published at GA46 pp. 523-526; approved by roll call with multiple dissents, source lines 15-23.
evidence_notes.dispute: The majority states only mootness. The dissent describes a dispute over session powers and a Nashville Presbytery ruling that the session erred and had to redress its actions, with some session and congregation members complaining; source lines 29-37.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC found circumstances rendered the complaint moot, source line 17, and gave no rationale in the majority order. The dissent says there was no record evidence of abandonment or withdrawal, that a filing-timeliness question should have been paneled, and that unexplained mootness would undermine the SJC; source lines 35-65.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The final disposition is mootness, not abandonment, dismissal, or a merits ruling. The dispute background and objections are from the dissent, not the adopted majority. McGowan disqualified himself as a Presbytery member; source lines 21-23, 35-65.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: None. No incorporated decision is supplied or relied on; related cases are mentioned only as the dissent's speculation about possible mootness rationales, source lines 45-47.

source_limits: The source is a short majority order; it does not include the complaint, the record, or the lower-court decision. The only description of the underlying dispute appears in the dissent, and the majority's mootness rationale is absent. The roll call lists concurrences and dissents, but there is no separate majority opinion.
